records.text: N1098L departed Biggs Army Airfield at a stated 6:13 a.m. and made a low pass of about 300 feet over the Provo Airport runway at 9:16 a.m.
records.speaker: Candace Owens

appearances.snippet: It was contracted by our military for whatever reason. This plane departed from the Biggs Army Airfield at 6:13 a.m. That's down in El Paso, Texas, right? ... And despite the fact that they were heading to Montana, they decided to make an unusual dip at 9:16 a.m. Again, this is in Utah time. ... They dipped down to just 300 feet above ground over the Provo airport runway, and they made a loop.
They dipped down to just 300 feet above ground over the Provo airport runway, and they made a loop.

verification.notes: Historical FlightAware material supports N1098L’s September 10 Biggs-to-Kalispell route and a low-altitude point near Provo at 9:16 a.m.; the preserved display reports 4,700 feet MSL, only a few hundred feet above the valley floor. However, the historical leg is 1348Z (7:48 a.m. MDT), not the stated 6:13 a.m. The route and low-pass component are supported, while the departure-time component is contradicted and exact AGL figures depend on interpreting the displayed MSL altitude.

records.speaker: Candace Owens

appearances.snippet: It was contracted by our military for whatever reason. This plane departed from the Biggs Army Airfield at 6:13 a.m. That's down in El Paso, Texas, right?

verification.notes: The aircraft and route are supported: FlightAware’s historical record identifies N1098L flying from Biggs AAF (KBIF) to Kalispell (KGPI) on September 10, 2025, and Leidos describes its contractor-operated Global 6500 Army ISR service. The exact time in the legacy claim is not supported: the historical leg is 1348Z, equivalent to 7:48 a.m. MDT, and a preserved FlightAware screenshot also reports 7:48 a.m., not 6:13 a.m. Thus the departure location/date is supported but the stated departure time is contradicted.
